R322_new_correction.flaw: R321's matched obstruction fractions did NOT match baseline hydraulic conductance. The distributed system with 5 open channels has R_distributed = R_channel/5. The single system at 50% obstruction has R_single = 2*R_channel. The distributed system has ~10x greater conductance. The pressure difference is explained by conductance difference, NOT by architectural redundancy.
R322_new_correction.math: Distributed 5/10: G = 5 * (π*D⁴/(128*μ*L)) = 5*G_channel. Single 50%: G = G_channel/2. Ratio = 10:1. The 7.6x pressure difference is EXACTLY what you'd expect from 10x conductance difference. It does NOT prove the distributed architecture is inherently safer.

corrected_classification.MATCHED_BASELINE_HYDRAULIC_PERFORMANCE: NOT_PROVEN — baseline conductances were NOT matched. Distributed had ~10x more conductance.
corrected_classification.REDUNDANCY_MECHANISM: NOT_YET_ISOLATED — the experiment has not isolated redundancy from conductance retention.

R322_new_correction.what_R321_actually_proved: At matched obstruction FRACTION, the system with more surviving conductance has lower pressure. This is trivially true and does NOT prove architectural advantage.
R322_new_correction.what_R321_did_NOT_prove: That distributed architecture provides safety advantage BEYOND what a single channel of equivalent baseline conductance would provide under the same fractional loss.

R322_experiment_required.step_1: Calibrate single-channel diameter so baseline conductance matches distributed (D_single ≈ 1.78*D_distributed for 10 channels)
R322_experiment_required.step_2: Verify baseline pressure is matched (within tolerance) through svMultiPhysics
R322_experiment_required.step_3: Apply matched fractional obstruction to BOTH conductance-matched systems
R322_experiment_required.step_4: Compare pressure under obstruction — this isolates redundancy from conductance

permanent_machine_rule: BASELINE_CONDUCTANCE_MATCHING: When comparing architectures with different numbers of channels, baseline hydraulic conductance MUST be matched before applying obstruction. Comparing systems with different baseline conductance under matched obstruction fraction is confounded. This rule applies to ALL comparative hydraulic experiments.
